original_question: Find (or prove it does not exist) a complete hyperbolic manifold not biholomorphic to a convex domain where the Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances agree everywhere.
target_in_paper: Problem 7.5.5 in §7.5, “The Kobayashi Metric k”: “Find (or prove it does not exist) a complete hyperbolic manifold not biholomorphic to a convex domain where the Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances agree everywhere.” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially verbatim to the paper’s official problem statement: it asks for a complete hyperbolic manifold, excludes manifolds biholomorphic to a convex domain, and requires global equality of the Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone formulation, manifold should be made explicit as a complex manifold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))

The paper leaves complete hyperbolic implicit; to make the question self-contained, this should be unpacked as Kobayashi hyperbolic and complete with respect to the Kobayashi distance. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))
Agree everywhere should be written explicitly as k_M(p,q)=c_M(p,q) for all pairs of points p,q in M. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))

To avoid confusion with nearby Problem 7.3.2, the statement should specify that it concerns the global Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances, not merely comparability of the infinitesimal metrics. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))

The paper does not impose boundedness, smooth boundary, pseudoconvexity, Stein, or fixed-dimension hypotheses, so a faithful rewrite should not add any such restrictions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))
If convex domain is expanded for self-containment, it should mean a convex domain in some C^N; the paper does not fix N. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))
refined_question: Does there exist a complete hyperbolic complex manifold M (that is, M is Kobayashi hyperbolic and complete for its Kobayashi distance k_M) such that k_M(p,q)=c_M(p,q) for every p,q in M, yet M is not biholomorphic to any convex domain in some C^N? If such an M exists, construct one; otherwise prove that no such manifold exists. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 7.5.5 in §7.5, and your draft already matches it almost word for word. The only sharpening needed is to make explicit the ambient object and quantifiers that the problem list leaves implicit: complex manifold, completeness with respect to the Kobayashi distance, and equality for all pairs of points. Nearby Problem 7.3.2 is related but different: it asks only whether there is a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain on which the Kobayashi and Carathéodory metrics are not comparable. So broadening your draft into a general comparison problem would move away from the paper’s actual target. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9509202))
